<objective>
Add the seven `radix-nova` registry primitives this repo is missing, hand-author the two that have no
registry item, and bring all nine onto the Cena visual language at the 44px touch floor.

Purpose: `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` corrects the audit's arithmetic in both directions. The real surface is **19
primitives, not 16** — the repo also ships `alert`, `avatar` and `dropdown-menu`, which the imported
system never names and which would look mixed-system if left alone. The real net-new count is **6 CLI
adds plus 1 transitive (`separator`) plus 2 hand-authored**, because `IconButton` is already
`Button size="icon"` in four sizes and `Toast` is already `sonner`, which the registry has no entry to
replace. Two of the audit's "10 missing" were never missing.

Output: nine new primitive files, `label.tsx` verified intact, and the touch-floor gate extended.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It closes the net-new half of SC2's
primitive inventory. Plan 01.1-08 re-skins the ten that already exist.

**Nothing consumes these yet.** They are added before any surface uses them precisely so a red in plan
01.1-09 through 01.1-12 is unambiguously a surface problem.
</objective>

  </read_first>
  <action>
    Bring the seven onto the Cena visual language. This is a class-level change only — no behaviour, no
    prop signature and no accessible name moves.

    **The 44px floor, control by control.** For controls with a large painted box (`select` trigger,
    `tabs` trigger, `tooltip` trigger wrapper, `field` rows), set the painted height to at least 44px
    directly. For small painted controls where growing the box would be visually wrong — `radio-group`
    items and the `switch` thumb track — **expand the pseudo-element and keep the visual box small**, which
    is the pattern `checkbox.tsx` already establishes. Note that `checkbox.tsx`'s current expander reaches
    only about 40×40 on a `size-4` box; the correct inset to reach 44 from a 16px box is 14px on each axis.
    Apply that inset to the new controls here; `checkbox.tsx` itself is corrected in plan 01.1-08.

    **Keep Radix state semantics.** A re-skin styles the state selector; it does not replace the state
    model. `radio-group` and `switch` arrive using the same shorthand form `checkbox.tsx` uses — leave it
    alone. Do not normalise it to the long attribute-selector form.

    **Colour discipline.** Azure appears **once per view as the primary action**, so no primitive in this
    set takes an accent fill by default. Accent is reserved for: the single primary CTA on a screen, the
    active or selected nav item, the active category chip and active dietary filter, the selected variant
    row, the "Clear filters" text link, the focus ring, and a momentary PIN-key press. Accent is **not**
    used for icons in general, links in body copy, secondary or tertiary buttons, status badges, sold-out
    badges, allergen or dietary chips, or any destructive control. Concretely: `switch` and
    `radio-group` take the accent only in their checked state; `tabs` takes it only on the active trigger;
    `select` and `tooltip` take it only on the focus ring. Control boundaries use the control-border token,
    not the decorative rule token — the two clear different WCAG thresholds and must not be collapsed.

    **`select` is added but not adopted on the venue form.** `radix-nova`'s `select` is a styled listbox; on
    a phone the native control opens the OS picker, which is strictly better one-handed. The venue form
    keeps its two native controls. Record that in `components/ui/select.tsx`'s header so a later reader
    does not "finish the migration" by swapping them.

    **Do not add the client-boundary directive to `separator`** — it renders no Radix state and adding it
    would push consuming Server Components to the client.

    Then **extend `tests/theme/touch-targets.test.ts`** rather than writing a second file. The existing
    test derives its assertion table from source; add the new primitives to that derivation so each is
    checked for either a painted height of at least 44px or a hit expander that reaches 44px. Keep the
    non-vacuity guard and raise its minimum to match the larger table. Record in the header that
    display-only elements are exempt — PIN dot indicators, non-filter allergen and dietary chips, status
    badges, the sold-out badge — but that a dietary **filter** chip is a control and is not exempt.

    Observe the extended test failing once, by temporarily setting one new control below the floor, before
    accepting it.
  </action>

<task type="auto">
  <name>Task 3: Hand-author Icon and Tag — the two primitives with no registry item</name>
  <files>components/ui/icon.tsx, components/ui/tag.tsx</files>
  <read_first>
    - `components/ui/label.tsx` — the minimal-wrapper shape `icon.tsx` follows (a short pass-through with `cn`)
    - `components/ui/badge.tsx` in full — the exact analog for `tag.tsx`: same cva shape minus `size`, rendering a `<span>`, `h-5 … rounded-4xl px-2 py-0.5 text-xs`. Note it composes `className` OUTSIDE the cva call where `button.tsx` passes it INSIDE
    - `components/ui/checkbox.tsx` lines 7 and 26, `components/ui/dialog.tsx` line 8, `components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx` line 7, `components/ui/sonner.tsx` line 5 — the four in-primitive glyph import sites, and the parent-selector sizing convention (`[&>svg]:size-3.5`, `[&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-4`) used instead of props
    - `app/tokens/cena.css` (plan 01.1-05) — the warning token trio the napfeny variant uses
    - `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/01.1-UI-SPEC.md` §§ "Design System" (the 1.75 stroke row), "The napfeny rule", "New — unverified-AI-field marking (INGEST-04/06)"
  </read_first>
  <action>
    Two small files.

    **`components/ui/icon.tsx`.** A wrapper that pins the design system's stroke weight. The imported
    system's 50 glyphs *are* Lucide, drawn at 1.75 rather than Lucide's stock 2 — so the fix is a stroke
    convention, not a second icon set. Accept a Lucide component as a prop plus the usual `className` and
    spread, render it with `strokeWidth` defaulting to `1.75` and a `data-slot="icon"` attribute, and
    default the size to `size-4` through `cn()` so a caller's explicit size still wins. Keep it to roughly
    fifteen lines and take the `LucideIcon` type as a type-only import. Do not add the client-boundary
    directive — this renders no state, and adding it would push consuming Server Components to the client.

    Record in the header that this is an **eighteen-file migration, not a one-file addition**: eighteen
    files across the repo import glyphs directly from `lucide-react` today and none sets a stroke weight.
    Those call sites are migrated by the plans that already touch each file — plan 01.1-08 for
    `checkbox.tsx`, `dialog.tsx`, `dropdown-menu.tsx` and `sonner.tsx`, and plans 01.1-09 through 01.1-12
    for the fourteen surfaces — and plan 01.1-14 adds the discipline test that proves the migration is
    complete. Doing it as one eighteen-file task was considered and rejected: it would conflict on files
    with three surface plans running in the same wave.

    **`components/ui/tag.tsx`.** A static chip with no Radix behaviour, following `badge.tsx`'s cva shape.
    Render a `<span>` with `data-slot="tag"` and `data-variant` mirroring the cva prop. Compose `className`
    **inside** the cva call, matching `button.tsx` — `twMerge` makes both placements behave identically, but
    the repo should read consistently and `button.tsx` is the canonical file. Record that choice in the header.

    Ship at least three variants. `default` — the neutral chip on the chip surface, which is what an
    allergen chip uses: muted ink on the chip surface, measured 4.96:1, rendered at the Label role (14px),
    **never at 10px**. `accent` — for dietary tags: accent ink on the accent-soft surface, uppercase Label.
    `warning` — the napfeny unverified-AI-field marker: warning-soft fill, a 1px warning-border rule,
    warning-ink Label text, sized to sit beside a 14px alert-triangle glyph.

    Two contract points for the header. **Text on the napfeny fill is always the warning ink** — never
    black, never the body ink. And **gold is capped at roughly 5% of any screen and is never a surface**:
    in v1 it appears in exactly three places — the "Now" badge on the currently-live menu, the last-good
    offline banner, and this marker — so a `Tag` in the warning variant counts against that cap.

    Allergen and dietary chips that are **not** filter controls are display-only and exempt from the 44px
    floor. A dietary **filter** chip is a control and is not exempt; it is built in Phase 3 on `Button` or
    on a toggle, not on this `Tag`. Say so in the header.

    A seventh `Badge` variant was considered instead of a separate file and rejected: the napfeny marker
    needs a border rule and an icon slot that `badge.tsx`'s shape does not carry, and a distinct
    `data-slot` makes the marker greppable for the INGEST-06 publish gate.
  </action>
  <verify>

**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| shadcn registry → repo source | `shadcn add` copies `.tsx` files into `components/ui/` where they become repo code executed in production. |
| CLI → existing repo file | `field` pulls `label` as a registry dependency and `label.tsx` already exists. |
